text:
**Answer**

The party that represents Oklahoma’s U.S. senators—the **Republican Party**—has been in control of both the U.S. House Rules Committee and the U.S. Senate Rules & Administration Committee since the start of the **114th Congress** on **January 3, 2015**.

**Why**

* **House Rules Committee** – When the 114th Congress convened on Jan. 3 2015, the Republicans gained the majority in the House for the first time since the 107th Congress. Consequently, the chair of the House Rules Committee became the Republican Rep. Pete Sessions, and the committee’s 9–9 majority (9 Republicans, 4 Democrats) was established.

* **Senate Rules & Administration Committee** – Likewise, the Republicans took the majority in the Senate in the 2014 elections and assumed control of the Senate when the 114th Congress opened. The chair of the Senate Rules & Administration Committee was the Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell, and the committee’s party ratio reflected the new majority (9 Republicans, 8 Democrats).

Thus, since **January 3 2015** the Republican Party—Oklahoma’s party—has held control of the committees that set the rules for both chambers of Congress.

**Answer**

The party that represents Oklahoma’s U.S. senators—the **Republican Party**—has been in control of both the U.S. House Rules Committee and the U.S. Senate Rules & Administration Committee since the start of the **114th Congress** on **January 3, 2015**.

**Why**

* **House Rules Committee** – When the 114th Congress convened on Jan. 3 2015, the Republicans gained the majority in the House for the first time since the 107th Congress. Consequently, the chair of the House Rules Committee became the Republican Rep. Pete Sessions, and the committee’s 9–9 majority (9 Republicans, 4 Democrats) was established.

* **Senate Rules & Administration Committee** – Likewise, the Republicans took the majority in the Senate in the 2014 elections and assumed control of the Senate when the 114th Congress opened. The chair of the Senate Rules & Administration Committee was the Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell, and the committee’s party ratio reflected the new majority (9 Republicans, 8 Democrats).

Thus, since **January 3 2015** the Republican Party—Oklahoma’s party—has held control of the committees that set the rules for both chambers of Congress.
